title: Chess, But SCP-409 FREEZES Your Pieces
summary: Standard chess vs Stockfish with neutral SCP-409 (the crystal) starting on c4. The crystal alternates between moving one square and crystallizing every piece in its 1-square radius. Crystallized pieces are frozen (cannot move, and do not defend/attack) for three turns, after which each has a 50% chance to defrost and a 50% chance to vanish from the board. Pawns that are blocked cannot escape; other pieces get one turn of warning. Narrator wins game one by checkmate once the crystal freezes Black's pieces.
rules: Standard chess otherwise; player White vs Stockfish (3600) Black.
Neutral SCP-409 crystal starts on c4; it cannot be captured [inferred].

The crystal alternates rounds: one round it moves one square (random wander), the next round it crystallizes all pieces on its 8 adjacent squares. Pieces adjacent after it moves therefore have one turn to step away.
Crystallized pieces cannot move and do not actively defend or attack squares ('it doesn't actively defend E5 on this turn'); they can still be captured.
Three turns after being crystallized, each crystallized piece independently has 50% chance to defrost (return to normal) and 50% chance to disappear from the board.
A crystallized king would be removed with 50% chance, ending the game [narrator's hope; not shown].
